findings.title: No guides exist for ad-hoc work outside a git project
findings.why_it_matters: harness-snapshot.json shows both instructions.CLAUDE.md and instructions.AGENT.md as null at the home directory level. Every session run directly in $HOME (not inside a specific project with its own CLAUDE.md) starts with zero standing instructions — no coding conventions, no default posture on autonomy, nothing. 7 of the 12 sessions analyzed were run this way. Compare this to the workshop project's own harness, which at least has (contradictory, but present) CLAUDE.md/AGENT.md guides.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal ~/CLAUDE.md with whatever's true across all your ad-hoc work regardless of project (e.g. default shell/OS notes, a preference on autonomy/confirmation before destructive actions, pointers to where scratch work should live).

findings.title: Zero sensors registered at the home level
findings.why_it_matters: harness-snapshot.json's hooks array is empty and hooks_not_observable is empty in index.json — there is no PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, or UserPromptSubmit hook of any kind. Nothing automatically catches a repeated failure, logs a decision, or gates a risky action before or after the agent acts. This matters concretely here: 3 sessions (3b902266, f51fa26f, a3c3d2d2, see finding #4) had the same tool fail more than once in a row, and nothing in the harness flagged that pattern — a human had to notice and intervene live each time.
findings.recommendation: Add at least one global sensor — even a simple Stop hook that flags when the same tool errored 2+ times in one turn sequence would have caught the exact pattern in finding #4 automatically instead of relying on live attention.

findings.title: The one guide that does exist (permissions) is degraded to the point of being meaningless
findings.why_it_matters: The allow-list has 105 entries. 16 of them are corrupted artifacts of the form 'Bash(__NEW_LINE_8a90271c2d057779__ grep:*)' — leftovers from some past multi-line command approval that got mis-parsed into garbage patterns that will never match a real command again. More importantly, the list ends with a bare 'Bash(*)', which grants blanket approval for any shell command whatsoever — this makes every other entry in the list redundant, since an unrestricted wildcard already permits everything a narrower pattern would. The permissions guide is not narrowing anything; it's decorative.
findings.recommendation: Remove the 16 corrupted __NEW_LINE_ entries. Replace the trailing Bash(*) with a real, bounded set of pre-approved patterns (the way the rest of the list was clearly originally intended to work) so the allowlist actually constrains what runs without confirmation.

findings.title: Three sessions show a confirmed denial followed by the same tool failing again
findings.harness_component: no guide steered the agent away from repeating the denied action, and no sensor caught the repeat
findings.why_it_matters: All three permission_denials in the dataset carry confidence: "confirmed" (Claude Code's exact rejection boilerplate, not a keyword guess) — these are real moments the user had to stop the agent: a PowerShell command, an AskUserQuestion call, and a Playwright browser_navigate call. In every one of these three sessions, the same tool (PowerShell, Artifact, and Bash respectively) then shows up in repeated_failed_tools — the agent kept hitting friction with that tool after being corrected once. This is the concrete cost of findings #1 and #2 combined: no guide narrowed the agent's approach after correction, and no sensor caught the repeat automatically.
findings.recommendation: See recommendations for findings #1 and #2 — this is the evidence that those gaps have a real, repeated cost, not just a theoretical one.

findings.title: The same task was started twice in one day
findings.harness_component: no persisted state/handoff between related sessions
findings.why_it_matters: Both sessions are dated 2026-08-26 and are explicitly about the same task: 'Agent harness workshop template' and 'Agent harness workshop template repository,' the second one's first prompt being 'You will help me create a GitHub repository that serves as a template codebase for a workshop on improving an agent harness...'. Without a guide that persists what was already decided/built in the first attempt, the second session has to re-establish the same context and intent from scratch.
findings.recommendation: For multi-session efforts on the same deliverable, keep a short running note (even a plan file or a project-local CLAUDE.md once the repo exists) that the next session can pick up from, instead of re-describing the goal from zero.
